extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing statutory invention registrations (SIR), eighteen-month (pre-grant) publication of patent applications, content/timing/format requirements for publications, and treatment/filing requirements for third‑party preissuance submissions under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)/(e) and 37 CFR 1.211/1.215/1.290.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of Statutory Invention Registration (SIR) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Only requests for a statutory invention registration filed prior to March 16, 2013 are timely; requests filed on or after March 16, 2013 will not be treated as pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 157 was repealed effective that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on requests filed before March 16, 2013 is found in earlier MPEP revisions; material in former MPEP §§1103-1109 is not repeated in this edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and public statement of published SIRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each published SIR will include a statement that 'A statutory invention registration is not a patent. It has the defensive attributes of a patent but does not have the enforceable attributes of a patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published SIRs are sequentially numbered in an 'H' series (H1, ...). No article or advertisement may use the term 'patent' or any suggestive term when referring to a SIR. For rights associated see 35 U.S.C. 157.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of SIR as prior art and constructive reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A published SIR will be treated the same as a U.S. patent for all defensive purposes and usable as a reference as of its filing date; a SIR is a 'constructive reduction to practice' under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) and 'prior art' under applicable sections of 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIRs are classified, cross-referenced, placed in search files, disseminated to foreign patent offices, stored in USPTO databases, made available in commercial databases, and announced in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of patent rights upon SIR publication and its impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Waiver of patent rights to subject matter claimed in a SIR takes effect on publication and may affect patentability of claims in related applications; waiver applies to any inventions claimed in the SIR and may preclude patenting by the same inventor in related applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply standards similar to 'same invention' double patenting determinations to decide if waiver precludes patenting. Rejection due to waiver cannot be overcome by a terminal disclaimer. The holder of a SIR cannot file a reissue to recapture waived rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighteen‑month publication general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, each U.S. national application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and international applications under 35 U.S.C. 371 will be published promptly after 18 months from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At applicant's request, an application may be published earlier than the 18‑month period. Director's determinations on release of published application information are final and nonreviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to eighteen‑month publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will not be published if it is (i) no longer pending, (ii) subject to a secrecy order or national security classification, (iii) a provisional application, or (iv) an application for a design patent (and certain reissue/design international cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not publish provisional applications, design applications, international design applications, or reissue applications under specified statutes. For practical avoidance of publication by abandonment, a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness required for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will not be published (or publication may be delayed) unless it includes the basic filing fee and any required English translation; the Office may also delay publication until other items are present (size fee, compliant specification, abstract, drawings, sequence listing, executed oath/declaration or ADS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required content is missing or of insufficient quality, the Office will issue a preexamination notice requiring replacement papers; publication will occur as soon as practical after deficiencies are corrected. Delaying necessary content to avoid publication may reduce patent term adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office refusal to include portions or refuse publication for legal or offensive content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may refuse to publish an application, or include a portion of an application in the publication, if publication would violate federal or state law or if the application (or portion) contains offensive or disparaging material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require a substitute specification to delete unlawful or offensive portions. See 37 CFR 1.211(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee and payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication fee set in 37 CFR 1.18(d) must be paid in each application published under 37 CFR 1.211 before the patent will be granted; the fee is included in the notice of allowance and must be paid within three months from mailing of the notice of allowance to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three‑month payment period is not extendable. If the application is not published under 37 CFR 1.211, any publication fee paid will be refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected publication date and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the application is complete, the Office will provide a projected publication date on the filing receipt, normally the later of: (1) eighteen months from earliest filing date claimed; or (2) fourteen weeks from the mailing date of the filing receipt. Technical preparations start about four months before publication; the publication process takes about fourteen weeks and publication occurs weekly (Thursday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should promptly review and correct filing receipt information and priority/benefit claims before technical preparations begin to avoid petitions and surcharges. If corrections are not recognized before technical prep begins, the projected publication date and published content may not be changeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the patent application publication (what is published)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication will be based upon the specification and drawings deposited on the filing date of the application, the application data sheet and/or the inventor's oath/declaration; it may also include timely amendments to the specification (other than abstract/claims), amendments to abstract, complete claim listings, and amended drawings if submitted in time for technical preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may provide an electronic copy (EFS) of the amended application within one month of the first Office communication including a confirmation number or within fourteen months of earliest filing date, whichever is later, to have the publication based on the amended copy. The Office will attempt to use applicant-submitted amendments but cannot guarantee inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information inclusion in publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application publication will include the name of the assignee or person showing proprietary interest if that information is provided in the application data sheet in sufficient time to be entered before technical preparations begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignee information in the ADS for publication does not substitute for recording an assignment under part 3 of the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments timing and EFS copy for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments intended to be used for publication must be submitted in sufficient time to be entered into the file wrapper before technical preparations begin (generally four months prior to projected publication); alternately, a compliant EFS copy submitted within prescribed time windows will be used to create the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the EFS copy does not comply with EFS requirements, the Office will publish the application based on the originally filed papers unless publication process has not started and the Office elects to use the untimely copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance to avoid preliminary amendments at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not file preliminary amendments with the application; submitting no preliminary amendment reduces Office processing and helps ensure publications are printed correctly. A preliminary amendment present on filing is part of the original disclosure and may require substitute specification if not in a publishable format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where desired amendments exist, applicants should incorporate them into the text of the specification (including a new claim set) rather than submitting preliminary amendments. For continuation/divisional applications, new specification plus reference to prior oath/declaration may be used if no new matter is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for republication to correct publication errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections to publication errors and inclusion of desired amendments into the originally-filed text require a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.221(a); such errors will not be corrected by a corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §1130 for details on republication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices and sequence listing printing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices other than sequence listings or certain tables are not printed if they are on pages located after the claims; long nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings are not printed in the publication but published electronically with a statement and hyperlink in the patent application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer program listings may be printed if included before the claims; program listings on compact disc per 37 CFR 1.96(c) and 1.52(e) are not printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting to provisional or other status to avoid publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting a nonprovisional application to a provisional will not avoid publication of the nonprovisional application unless the conversion is recognized in sufficient time to remove the application from the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because technical preparations begin about four months before publication, applicants risking late recognition may still be published. To avoid publication by abandonment, applicants should file a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) for express abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party preissuance submission compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Third‑party submissions under 37 CFR 1.290 must comply with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and the procedural requirements of 37 CFR 1.290; the Office will screen submissions for compliance before entry into the application file wrapper (IFW).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any part of a submission is non‑compliant with 35 U.S.C. 122(e), the entire submission will not be entered. Errors purely in 37 CFR 1.290 requirements may be tolerated if minor and the content is readily ascertainable, at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and filing channel for third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Third‑party submissions should be filed electronically via the dedicated Web‑based interface for preissuance submissions; they may also be filed in paper via USPS first-class mail, Priority Mail Express, or hand delivery using form PTO/SB/429 (or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file third‑party submissions by facsimile. When filing electronically, use the dedicated interface and not the 'Document/Fees for an existing application/proceeding' option. Paper submissions incur additional scanning/indexing delay. A self-addressed postcard may be included to receive an acknowledgment of receipt but does not indicate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for third‑party submissions (concise descriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document listed in a third‑party submission must be accompanied by a concise description of the relevance of the document to the claims; lack of a concise description of relevance is a ground for non‑compliance and will prevent entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An improper concise description (e.g., not explaining relevance) or other content defects will be noted in a notification to the third party. The statutory time period for making a submission is not tolled by an initial non‑compliant filing; resubmissions may be made if the statutory window remains open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non‑compliant third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Non‑compliant third‑party submissions (except minor errors) will not be entered into the IFW, will not be considered, may be discarded, and required fees will not be refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will notify the third party of reasons for non‑compliance (e.g., missing concise descriptions, untimely filing). The Office will not set a period for correction; a correct complete submission may be filed if the statutory time period has not closed. Fee may be required for resubmission after a non‑compliance finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No third‑party participation after filing beyond submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The involvement of a third party ends with the filing of the submission; the third party will not receive communications from the Office regarding the submission other than the electronic acknowledgment, return postcard (if provided), or a notification regarding compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third party is not permitted to contact the examiner or respond to the examiner's treatment of the submission; prosecution is ex parte and no third‑party responses are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification practices for third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may request courtesy email notification regarding whether its submission was found compliant or non‑compliant by providing an email address when filing; no notification is issued if an email address is not provided or where the submission concerns an unpublished application (confidential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification will not be made of record in the application and the Office does not intend to enter the provided email address into the application record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and examiner treatment of entered third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: After a compliant third‑party submission is entered, the applicant (where participating in e-Office Action) will be notified and the contents will be made available via private PAIR; the examiner should consider the listed publications and concise descriptions generally before issuing the next Office action, treating them similarly to an IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should sign PTO/SB/429 to indicate consideration, clear the IDS flag in PALM, and provide a signed copy with the next Office action. The examiner’s signature indicates consideration only, not agreement with the third party's view. There is no need for the examiner to comment on concise descriptions in the Office action, but may apply the information as needed (e.g., rejecting claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and printing of documents cited by third‑parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents from a third‑party submission that were considered by the examiner will be printed on the patent and will be distinguished from documents cited by the applicant or examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner believes a listed document is not a publication, the examiner should consult the screener or TC point of contact and, if appropriate, strike through the document to indicate it was not considered; in some cases a stricken document may still be cited by the examiner on a form PTO‑892.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office screening and processing structure for third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Third‑party submissions will be screened for compliance by Office‑designated personnel (points of contact in each Technology Center) prior to entry into the IFW; paper filings will experience additional processing delay due to scanning and indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliant electronic submissions via the dedicated interface receive immediate electronic acknowledgment and are the most efficient means to make submissions available to an examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on filing channels and document options
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and third parties must file preissuance submissions using the dedicated electronic interface (or proper paper channel); applicants/representatives must not use the 'Document/Fees for an existing application/proceeding' option or the dedicated third‑party submission option incorrectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Office’s published instructions for form use and EFS-Web filing conventions to ensure timely and proper entry; improper filing option choice may render submission non‑compliant or cause delay.
